# Creating a *more*
# *food secure* world

Our planet’s population is growing rapidly — and so is the need for more food. Already, 800 million
people go to bed hungry each night. As a food company to the world, Cargill is partnering with
farmers and customers to grow and produce more food with less impact, to move that food to store
shelves and family tables, and to nourish people for a more food secure world.

[Watch the video][52]

**GROW**

### [Meet the farmers building our food-secure world][53]

**MOVE**

### [Advancing decarbonization across the food supply chain][54]

**NOURISH**

### [Discover how we’re building resilient food systems][55]

## 2025 Annual Report

#### Connecting a food secure world

The food you eat has a story to tell. Because before you take that first bite, a global network of
hard-working people – spanning countries, cultures and skillsets – each did their part to grow, make
and move your meal from where it was grown to the fork in your hand. At Cargill, it’s our privilege
to facilitate the complex connections that make it all happen.

In Cargill’s 2025 Annual Report, we share how we’re strengthening ties between farmers, frontline
food workers and the customers we exist to serve. Learn how our collective efforts are helping
transform food and agriculture and connect a food secure world.

[Read the Report][56]

[2025 annual report feature image]

 

 

[2025 Impact report feature image]

## 2025 Impact Report

#### Building a more resilient food system

As a company that sits at the center of the global food system, Cargill plays a unique role in
connecting farmers, food producers, and consumers. This vantage point makes it clear that the future
of food depends on a system that is productive, sustainable, and resilient.

In Cargill’s 2025 Impact Report, we share how our strategy reflects this interconnected view — how
growing food impacts natural resources; how it moves from where it’s grown; and how we partner to
expand access to nutrition, improve farmer and community livelihoods, and accelerate our customers’
progress on sustainability.

Together, we’re working to build a stronger, more sustainable food system that can nourish the world
for generations to come.

[Read the Report][57]

 

 

## Our purpose

#### To nourish the world in a safe, responsible and sustainable way

Sitting at the heart of the global supply chain, we join farmers, ranchers, manufacturers,
foodservice customers and retailers in sourcing, making and delivering products that are vital for
living.

Every day, our 155K+ team members come to work:
* Driven to improve lives through food, nutrition and health
* Looking for ways to innovate with purpose
* Committed to nourishing our growing world by providing access to life’s essentials

This is how we create new opportunities for our customers to grow, communities to prosper and
consumers to live well.

[Read about Cargill][58]

[Our purpose]

 

 

 

 

## People

 

With 155K+ colleagues in 70 countries, we work as a global network to bring together the people,
ideas and resources that can nourish lives around the world.

[Careers][59]

## Products

 

Partnering across the supply chain, we bring food, ingredients, agricultural solutions and
industrial products to meet customers’ ever-evolving needs.

[Products & Services][60]

## Planet

 

From small family farms to global shipping lanes, we work every day to bring new sustainable
practices, reduce our impact on the planet and take care of people.

[Sustainability][61]

# Someday our kids will design the living world

In our vision of the future, our children will program biology like we once programmed computers. In
that world, they will cure all diseases and grow everything they can imagine.

[Let's grow][17]
[Ginkgo bioworks imagery on new york stock exchange building ]

## Labwork is the bottleneck for biotechnology

Autonomous labs are the answer

Science still runs on manual benchwork, and that bottleneck slows progress on everything from novel
materials to lifesaving medicines. Autonomous labs replace the bench, letting scientists order
experimental work from robots just by asking for it.

This shift doesn’t replace scientists; it empowers them to focus on insight, creativity, and
judgment rather than manual lab work.

[What is an autonomous lab?][18]

# Creating a *more*
# *food secure* world

Our planet’s population is growing rapidly — and so is the need for more food. Already, 800 million
people go to bed hungry each night. As a food company to the world, Cargill is partnering with
farmers and customers to grow and produce more food with less impact, to move that food to store
shelves and family tables, and to nourish people for a more food secure world.

[Watch the video][52]

**GROW**

### [Meet the farmers building our food-secure world][53]

**MOVE**

### [Advancing decarbonization across the food supply chain][54]

**NOURISH**

### [Discover how we’re building resilient food systems][55]

## 2025 Annual Report

#### Connecting a food secure world

The food you eat has a story to tell. Because before you take that first bite, a global network of
hard-working people – spanning countries, cultures and skillsets – each did their part to grow, make
and move your meal from where it was grown to the fork in your hand. At Cargill, it’s our privilege
to facilitate the complex connections that make it all happen.

In Cargill’s 2025 Annual Report, we share how we’re strengthening ties between farmers, frontline
food workers and the customers we exist to serve. Learn how our collective efforts are helping
transform food and agriculture and connect a food secure world.

[Read the Report][56]

[2025 annual report feature image]

 

 

[2025 Impact report feature image]

## 2025 Impact Report

#### Building a more resilient food system

As a company that sits at the center of the global food system, Cargill plays a unique role in
connecting farmers, food producers, and consumers. This vantage point makes it clear that the future
of food depends on a system that is productive, sustainable, and resilient.

In Cargill’s 2025 Impact Report, we share how our strategy reflects this interconnected view — how
growing food impacts natural resources; how it moves from where it’s grown; and how we partner to
expand access to nutrition, improve farmer and community livelihoods, and accelerate our customers’
progress on sustainability.

Together, we’re working to build a stronger, more sustainable food system that can nourish the world
for generations to come.

[Read the Report][57]

 

 

## Our purpose

#### To nourish the world in a safe, responsible and sustainable way

Sitting at the heart of the global supply chain, we join farmers, ranchers, manufacturers,
foodservice customers and retailers in sourcing, making and delivering products that are vital for
living.

Every day, our 155K+ team members come to work:
* Driven to improve lives through food, nutrition and health
* Looking for ways to innovate with purpose
* Committed to nourishing our growing world by providing access to life’s essentials

This is how we create new opportunities for our customers to grow, communities to prosper and
consumers to live well.

[Read about Cargill][58]

[Our purpose]

 

 

 

 

## People

 

With 155K+ colleagues in 70 countries, we work as a global network to bring together the people,
ideas and resources that can nourish lives around the world.

[Careers][59]

## Products

 

Partnering across the supply chain, we bring food, ingredients, agricultural solutions and
industrial products to meet customers’ ever-evolving needs.

[Products & Services][60]

## Planet

 

From small family farms to global shipping lanes, we work every day to bring new sustainable
practices, reduce our impact on the planet and take care of people.

[Sustainability][61]

#### Geno is The Sustainable Source™

## making

## a material

## difference

We are accelerating the world's transformation to sustainable materials by replacing fossil fuel
sources with plants. We believe that all products should be responsibly sourced, traceable and
transparent — the sustainable source™.

## to us,

## less is more

Our technology has the capacity to reduce 85M tons of carbon per year. Our first technology is
already enabling up to 90% lower carbon emissions than the same products made using fossil fuels and
other unsustainable sources.

## to us,

## less is more

90% less CO2

with Geno BDO™, compared to coal-based alternatives.

## the

## planet has a

## dependency

We have a fossil fuel dependency. And our reliance extends far deeper than just fuel for our cars
and energy for our homes. Over the last 100 years, a vast array of molecules made from fossil fuels
have been the building blocks for much of modern life — from the materials in the clothing we wear
to the ingredients we put on our skin, to the medicines and foods we consume. Fossil fuels such as
crude oil and coal have had their day; for both environmental and geopolitical reasons, we need to
transition to more sustainable sources.

## the planet

## has a

## dependency

## climate

## change

## agent

At Geno, we are breaking the planet's reliance on these fossil fuels by creating something better.
Our vision to drive climate action at scale starts by making the same molecules, ingredients and
materials we rely on every day, but deriving them from more sustainable sources.

## same

## material,

## just better

We’re addressing the climate crisis by changing the ingredients that make up the products we use
every day.

## changing

## what the world

## is made of

## changing what

## the world is

## made of

Spanning products across a wide variety of industries, Geno’s technologies power high performance at
leading scale and volume, delivering plant-derived ingredients to some of the world’s largest
brands. And with that, we are shaping the creation of more transparent, traceable and responsible
global supply chains for brands and their consumers to rely on.

huge breakthroughs, many diseases, such as cancer, rheumatism or Alzheimer's, are still not

protect and enhance our planet. Headquartered in Switzerland, we are a global agritech leader with
more than 30,000 employees across over 90 countries.**

# Your Trusted Source for Security, AV and Smart Living Solutions

ADI is a leading distributor and solution provider of security, AV, and smart living products
serving over 100,000 customers worldwide. We offer access to a broad portfolio of products,
including top-tier distributed brands and our own exclusive brands.

With more than three decades of industry experience, we're committed to building long-lasting
customer relationships - making us a preferred partner for professionals across the industry.

# Our Mission

### We aim to provide products, services and software that help keep our communities safe, secure,
### comfortable and connected.

## Here's How We Do It

### Access to Exclusive Brands

We take pride in our exclusive, in-house manufactured products and software solutions, delivering
smart solutions that combine quality and innovation. From home automation to commercial-grade
infrastructure, we craft technologies that focus on what customers value most – delivering a

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
The degree course in Biosciences and Biotechnology is an interclass course that includes two        
distinct training paths at the end of which the student can graduate as a biologist or as a         
biotechnologist. Both paths make strong use of the reciprocal interaction between the themes of     
biology and the most recent acquisitions in the biotechnology field. The result is a flexible and   
modern course, closer to the current training needs of biologists and biotechnologists and more     
responsive to the demands of the labour market. The degree course is taught in English at the       
University of Camerino.

# Advanced In Vitro, Ex Vivo, and 3D Human Tissue Models for Drug Testing and Research

**CTIBIOTECH **™** develops advanced 2D and 3D cell culture models, including organoids and human
tissue models, for pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and biomedical research.We provide custom research
services, preclinical testing solutions, and contract research (CRO) services to support drug
discovery, toxicity testing, and offer reliable alternatives to animal testing.**

### **For a better human world**

## About us

CTIBIOTECH™, leveraging **NAM (Novel Alternative Models)**, specializes in the development of
advanced 2D and 3D human tissue models, including tumor models and organoids, for pharmaceutical and
cosmetic applications. **NAM’s** approach enhances our **in vitro** and **ex vivo** platforms,
designed for drug screening, toxicity testing, and oncology research, supporting preclinical
development with predictive and human-relevant data. We also provide custom model development and
contract research services (CRO) tailored to the needs of biotech and pharmaceutical companies.

At CTIBIOTECH™, we believe in innovation for a healthier future. Our goal is to create accurate and
reliable human tissues that enable researchers and companies to better understand diseases, test
drugs, and develop new treatments. We use cutting-edge technologies, such as stem cells and 3D
printing, to create 3D tissue and cell models that realistically simulate the structure and function
of human tissues.

## Our Mission

testing, dermatology research, and safety evaluation. Our solutions enable skin penetration testing
and efficacy analysis without animal experimentation, providing reliable and human-relevant results
for cosmetic companies.

###### **Pharmaceutical innovation**

###### **and testing**

Our in vitro and ex vivo models, including cancer organoids and tumor micro environment systems,
support drug screening, efficacy testing, and personalized medicine approaches. We also offer
preclinical testing services and CRO solutions to assist pharmaceutical companies in accelerating
drug development.

###### **Buy cells and tissues**

Our biobank-derived human cells and tissues, including skin, hair, blood, and stem cells, support in
vitro and ex vivo drug testing, cosmetic and pharmaceutical product development, efficacy
evaluation, and preclinical research. We also offer contract research, collaborative projects, and
custom biosourcing services to help biotech and pharmaceutical companies accelerate innovation.

# Services

#### ESG DATA MANAGEMENT AS A SERVICE
* #### Design & Strategy
  
  Get tailored project management support for initiatives, including - developing an ESG data
  governance and pipeline strategy, designing a cost effective IT architecture for ESG data
  management, implementing custom solutions to manage your ESG data.
* #### Data Collection
  
  Project management support for initiatives including - aggregating ESG data sources, stakeholder
  engagement and coordination, automating primary data collection, implementing continuous data
  collection processes, and integrating ESG data into standard business processes and workflows.
* #### Data Processing
  
  Project support for buidling ESG data models and pipelines, Data definition manuals, ESG data
  transformation (ETL),
* #### Data Represenation
  
  Reporting and disclosure, Impact dashboards,

#### MATERIALITY ANALYSIS AS A SERVICE
* #### Value Chain & Stakeholder Analysis
  
  Map value chain, identify stakeholders, generate material topics
* #### IRO Identification & Analysis
  
  Identify, categorize and analyse impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs) quantify financial
  materiality of risks, assess materiality based on stakeholder feedback.
* #### Materiality Matrix Development
  
  Identify materiality thresholds, create materiality matrix, map data points to business strategy,
  plan communication with stakeholders.

#### SUSTAINABILITY IMPLEMENTATION AS A SERVICE
* #### Frameworks & Standards
  
  Comprehensive project support for target-setting initiatives like SBTi and CDP, reporting and
  disclosure initiatives like CSRD, GRI and sector-specific frameworks.
* #### Carbon Accounting
  
  Organisational and product carbon accounting initiatives, including scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG
  inventory, product carbon footprinting, product lifecycle analysis (LCA) etc.
* #### Climate Mitigation & Adaptation
  
  Design, planning and implementation of climate mitigation and adaptation projects including,
  energy efficiency, decarbonization, circular economy, carbon abatement and climate investments.

# Color Meanings – Discover the Power and Symbolism Behind Every Hue

[Color Meanings]

Colors play an exceptionally prominent role in our lives. They influence our thinking, inspire our
decision-making, and impact our moods. From causing changes to changing reactions, colors are more
powerful than we think. Depending on our interpretations, they can be used for both good and evil.
Fortunately, we have the power to welcome some colors and shun others. This guide will take you on a
journey through the exciting universe of color meanings.

It’s important to note that not all colors were created equal. Though some shades are similar, that
doesn’t mean they’ll awaken the same emotions. To truly grasp the meaning of color, we must learn to
accept this. It’s also imperative to relinquish some control. Try as we might, we won’t always have
a handle on our emotions. Colors have such a substantial effect on the mind and body, and until we
make our peace with this reality, we’ll remain forever perplexed by inexplicable and random
reactions.

## Recognizing Your Responses

Have you ever noticed a shift in your attitude while surrounded by a particular color? Perhaps
you’ve been overwhelmed with nostalgia while staring at a specific shade. You’ve likely written
these occurrences off as a common human response, but the cause is far more complex than that. Color
psychology teaches us that much of human behavior is dictated by color. When we open our minds to
this possibility, we begin to understand the scope of our perceptions.

## Personal Cognizance

Once we acknowledge that colors influence doings, it makes way for personal interpretations. In
other words, we level the playing field by regaining some control of how we react to colors. You may
realize that the color red triggers anger. To avoid unnecessary bouts of rage, limit your encounters
with this hue. On the other hand, yellow might make you feel cheery and upbeat. If so, introduce
more of this color into your life. With a healthy dose of awareness, you can somewhat manage the
moods and emotions that colors produce.

## Uncovering New Meanings

The psychology behind color is fascinating and ever-expanding. With that said, new meanings are
always coming to light. The more knowledge we acquire, the more informed we become. This prospect
promises great hope for future research.

What’s more, our minds are in a perpetual state of evolvement. In essence, though some colors have
fixed explanations, these findings can always shift. This fact is both unsettling and reassuring. As
researchers continue to delve into the many facets of the color wheel, new information is
continually revealing itself.

## Diversify Your Understandings

While reading these articles, you’ll develop a deeper understanding of what colors mean, how they
make an impression on us, and the ways we perceive them. The notion that colors are so dynamic may
seem absurd to some, but there’s no refuting this truth. This concept often eludes us because we
don’t realize how frequently colors control us. Certain hues can evoke fond memories. Others may
give rise to dreadful feelings.

*Posted on: 3 July 2026, source: medpagetoday*
The FDA on Wednesday expanded the approval for exagamglogene autotemcel (exa-cel, Casgevy) in severe
sickle cell disease with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises and transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia
to include children 2 years and up. Exa-cel, the first FDA-approved therapy utilizing CRISPR/Cas9
gene editing technology, was previously only approved for adults and pediatric patients 12 years and
older. The expanded indication makes exa-cel the first gene therapy approved for kids as young as 2
with these debilitating diseases.

## What is a HTML color code?

A HTML color code is an identifier used to represent a color on the web and within other digital
assets. Common color codes are in the forms of: a keyword name, a hexadecimal value, a RGB (red,
green, blue) triplet, or a HSL (hue, saturation, lightness) triplet. Different values allow for
16,777,216 potential colors to be chosen.

For example, the color red can be identifier using the following formats:
* red (keyword name)
* #ff0000 (hex)
* (255,0,0) (RGB)
* (0, 100%, 50%) (HSL)

Because there are so many colors to choose from, tools have been created to make the task of
selection much simpler. A color picker allows a user to select a color by clicking on visual range
of color to pin-point an exact code. A color chart provides a listing of common colors for quick
selection.

To use a selected color code within your web page, you could place the following attribute within a
given element to change its background color to red: `style="background-color: #ff0000;"`

## What are HTML color codes used for?

HTML color codes are used within HTML and CSS to create web design color schemes. They are primarily
used by web designers, graphic designers, computer programmers, and digital illustrators. Choosing
the correct web colors can be exhausting, but it is a great skill to have, especially for marketing
purposes.

To read more about html colors, Wikipedia has a good resource on web colors:
[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_colors][27].

assurance.

manufacturing sites. Led by Jörg Kampmeyer, Dr Uwe Knotzer, Dr Kristin Neumann and Murat Akyildiz,

employees worldwide.

## Overview of tools

[Technology Centre Mapping]

# [Technology Centre Mapping][54]

Technology Centres help SMEs cross the 'Valley of Death' and go from lab to market to develop and
produce new technology-based products. They help companies reduce the time-to-market for new
innovation ideas. The EMI technology centre mapping helps businesses locate technology centres
across the EU that can address their needs.

[EU Reports]

# [EU Reports][55]

The goal of the EMI EU report is to provide an overview about the green and digital transition of
industrial ecosystems and progress made over time. The report draws conclusions regarding the EU's
competitive standing in advanced-technology-driven ecosystems when compared to its primary global
rivals. The first EU report will be launched soon.

[International Reports]

# [International Reports][56]

International reports explore the positioning of third countries regarding the development and
implementation of advanced technologies across industrial ecosystems. The EMI international reports
are currently in development and will be published on this page when they are finalised.

[EU Member State Factsheets]

# [EU Member State Factsheets][57]

The EU Member State factsheets present key findings about the state-of-play of the green and digital
transition in each of the EU’s 27 Member States, based on patent, production, investment, and trade
data collected within the framework of the EMI project. The 27 EU Member State factsheets are now
available.

[Technology Centre Reports]

# [Technology Centre Reports][58]

Technology Centres, and the technology infrastructures they host, offer a wide range of services
such as access to technology expertise and facilities, demonstration, prototype development and
testing, among others, which make them vital actors to realise industrial policy objectives.
However, this contribution is not always visible. The EMI project has therefore produced two reports
which describe the role of Technology Centres in the development of innovation ecosystems and their
added value in addressing the needs of industry. These reports will be made available soon.

# Our certifications

OEKO-TEX® standards enable everyone to make responsible decisions and protect natural resources.
Driven by sustainability and a dedication to transparency, our work is grounded in proven science.
Explore our portfolio [here][69] or apply for your chosen certification or service. 

[
[OEKO-TEX® MADE IN GREEN certification]

The MADE IN GREEN label identifies textiles and leather goods tested for harmful substances and
which have been manufactured under sustainable and socially responsible conditions.

][70]
[
[OEKO-TEX® STANDARD 100 certification]

All types of textiles that have been tested for harmful substances, from yarns to the finished
product, may bear the STANDARD 100 product label.

][71]
[
[OEKO-TEX® ORGANIC COTTON certification]

The ORGANIC COTTON certification offers verification from farm to product. Products bearing this
label have been tested for the use of genetically modified organisms (GMOs) and harmful substances.
 

][72]
[
[OEKO-TEX® LEATHER STANDARD certification]

The LEATHER STANDARD label is tailored to leather articles which have been tested for harmful
substances. Certification can be awarded for leather semi-finished products, finished leather,
leather fibre materials up to finished articles and accessories.

][73]
[
[OEKO-TEX® STeP certification]

STeP certifies production facilities which manufacture textile and leather articles under
sustainable production conditions.

][74]
[
[OEKO-TEX® ECO PASSPORT certification]

The ECO PASSPORT identifies chemicals, colourants and auxiliaries used in the textile and leather
industry which are not harmful to health and which are environmentally friendly.

][75]
[
[OEKO-TEX® RESPONSIBLE BUSINESS certification]

RESPONSIBLE BUSINESS supports you on preventing or mitigating existing and potential negative
impacts of business operations within your own activities, your supply chains and your wider
business relationships. 

][76]

## Environmentally Friendly Marine Fuels for Global Shipping

TOO Qazaqstan Marine Fuels (QMF) is a Kazakh company dedicated to producing high-quality marine
fuels in strict accordance with the International Convention MARPOL 73/78 standards.

### Our Mission

We produce two types of environmentally friendly marine fuel from Kazakh ultra-low sulfur oil:
Marine fuel distillate DMA and Marine fuel residual RMD, both compliant with ISO 8217-2017
standards.

### Our Authority

With our founder as a subsoil user company (76% share), QMF holds official "Oil Supplier" status
under the Republic of Kazakhstan Law on State Regulation of Production and Circulation of Petroleum
Products. This enables us to process oil from both our parent company and other subsoil user
companies.

Hi! I’m Kate Smith, an internationally recognized color expert who’s been making color accessible
since 2001.



For over two decades, I’ve helped thousands of corporate clients, students, and companies worldwide
master color through proven, research-backed methodologies. My approach has been refined through 20+
years of real-world application with Fortune 500 companies and individual clients alike.



My mission is simple: help YOU understand color, create with confidence, and discover your unique
color sense-ability using the same proven methods that have transformed color outcomes for thousands
of professionals before you.

# Quebec, Your Destination of Choice for Accelerating Your Clinical Research Projects

### Quebec is proposing a fast, reliable and stable clinical research environment that is aligned
### with rigorous pharmaceutical industry standards in order to support the success of your projects
### and help realize your ambitions.

A [G7 leader][33] in clinical research, Canada has the greatest number of clinical trials
proportionately to its population. Quebec plays a key role as participant in [more than 40%][34] of
all clinical research projects carried out across Canada. Through the expertise of its teams and the
excellence of its health care system, Quebec stands out in all treatment fields and for all
indications.

## Learn About What Makes up Quebec’s Strength in Clinical Research

[
[icon-14175]

A highly efficient environment for faster clinical trial start-up

][35]
[
[icon-14178]

International-calibre expertise in support of your projects

][36]
[
[icon-14180]

A unique demographic and genetic profile

][37]

A highly efficient environment for faster clinical trial start-up Quebec offers an efficient
pan-Canadian regulatory framework, allowing Health Canada to approve a clinical trial application
within 30 days, and a [FAST TRACK Evaluation Service][38] aimed at approving clinical research
trials in 8 weeks in public institutions, which is about 75 % faster than the usual standard
timeframes found worldwide.

[World-class sites and investigators][39], [specialized contractual organizations][40], as well as [
patient organizations][41] driving the performance and quality of your projects.

Through its considerable ethnic diversity and some specific genetic characteristics inherited from a
small number of original inhabitants (called the “founder effect”), Quebec provides a unique context
for advancing research, particularly on rare diseases, orphan diseases and precision medicine. This
strength is maintained by a network of centres of excellence in rare diseases.

[
[icon-14182]

International recognition of clinical data in Quebec

][42]
[
[icon-14184]

Access to health data from a major integrated public network

][43]
[
[icon-14186]

Attractive tax incentives and credits

][44]

The trials conducted in Quebec observe Good Clinical Practices (GCP) and international standards,
ensuring that data generated are acceptable to agencies such as the FDA (USA) and EMA (Europe),
which facilitates access to world markets.

In the heart of one of the largest integrated health systems in North America, Quebec provides
[strategic access to anonymized health data for public and private research][45]. This access
enables faster and more precise clinical research that is rooted in real-world conditions, stepping
up the development and assessment of cutting-edge innovations.

Companies benefit from a provincial tax credit of up to 64 % of eligible salaries and 33 % of
subcontracting costs associated with scientific research and experimental development, in addition
to the federal tax credit. This tax support considerably reduces the total cost of pharmaceutical
development and medical technology projects.

## **Fédérer, innover, accélérer, développer**

[En savoir plus][60]
[Twb Logos Tutelles Inrae Insa Cnrs]

TWB valorise l’action des **micro-organismes comme catalyseurs de solutions industrielles nouvelles,
au service d’une industrie plus durable,** en mobilisant leur potentiel d’innovation.

### Notre ambition

Etre un acteur pionnier de la biotechnologie industrielle, couvrant toute la chaîne de valeur, **de
l’innovation de rupture aux bioprocédés pré-industriels.**

En s’appuyant sur son cœur de métier, des expertises de pointe, des plateformes avancées et un
écosystème multidisciplinaire, TWB intègre la modélisation et l’intelligence artificielle pour
accélérer l’innovation.

### **Une approche axée sur les synergies et l’agilité**

Faisant partie d’un écosystème d’innovation transdisciplinaire, TWB crée les synergies nécessaires
pour transformer rapidement les avancées scientifiques en applications industrielles concrètes en
**fédérant la diversité des acteurs et en proposant un accompagnement étayant pour les start-ups.**


**Collaborer avec TWB, c’est bénéficier d’un accompagnement agile et différenciant pour vos projets
de R&D.**

Les biotechnologies industrielles transforment la chimie en proposant des alternatives durables aux
procédés traditionnels, permettant la production de molécules d’intérêt via des micro-organismes ou
des enzymes.

TWB accompagne ces développements grâce à la** polyvalence de ses expertises **et à des **plateaux
analytiques en chimie et caractérisation cellulaire** disposant de technologies avancées.
À l’écoute des besoins du domaine de la chimie, TWB contribue à l’émergence d’une chimie plus verte,
performante et industrialisable.
* Transformer les effluents de l’industrie en molécules biosourcées,
* Réduire l’usage de solvants et de catalyseurs chimiques toxiques via des enzymes,
* Produire à grande échelle une molécule difficile à extraire,
* Sécuriser une supply chain fragile (plantes, extraction) ou réduire son impact sur

# Your Trusted Source for Security, AV and Smart Living Solutions

ADI is a leading distributor and solution provider of security, AV, and smart living products
serving over 100,000 customers worldwide. We offer access to a broad portfolio of products,
including top-tier distributed brands and our own exclusive brands.

With more than three decades of industry experience, we're committed to building long-lasting
customer relationships - making us a preferred partner for professionals across the industry.

# Our Mission

### We aim to provide products, services and software that help keep our communities safe, secure,
### comfortable and connected.

## Here's How We Do It

### Access to Exclusive Brands

We take pride in our exclusive, in-house manufactured products and software solutions, delivering
smart solutions that combine quality and innovation. From home automation to commercial-grade
infrastructure, we craft technologies that focus on what customers value most – delivering a
reliable and exceptional experience

[Access to Exclusive Brands]
[Support and Services]

### Support and Services

We offer a wide range of support and services to provide expert guidance at every step - from design
and configuration to ongoing support. With OvrC Remote Management, customers can easily manage,
configure, and troubleshoot devices across the network. OvrC is available on a range of exclusive
brand products and integrates with many leading distributed brands. Additional offerings include
systems design, technical support, rewards programs, training, project registration, and more.

### Robust Product Selection

With more than 500,000 products from over 1,000 trusted brands, ADI offers a carefully curated
selection of solutions to meet the needs for any application. We make purchasing easy - customers
can shop in-store or online and choose from multiple delivery options or in-store pickup.

[Robust Product Selection]

**B.Sc. in BIOSCIENCES & BIOTECHNOLOGY (L2/L13)**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
The degree course in Biosciences and Biotechnology is an interclass course that includes two        
distinct training paths at the end of which the student can graduate as a biologist or as a         
biotechnologist. Both paths make strong use of the reciprocal interaction between the themes of     
biology and the most recent acquisitions in the biotechnology field. The result is a flexible and   
modern course, closer to the current training needs of biologists and biotechnologists and more     
responsive to the demands of the labour market. The degree course is taught in English at the       
University of Camerino.

**B.Sc. in BIOSCIENCES & BIOTECHNOLOGY (L2/L13)**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
The degree course in Biosciences and Biotechnology is an interclass course that includes two        
distinct training paths at the end of which the student can graduate as a biologist or as a         
biotechnologist. Both paths make strong use of the reciprocal interaction between the themes of     
biology and the most recent acquisitions in the biotechnology field. The result is a flexible and   
modern course, closer to the current training needs of biologists and biotechnologists and more     
responsive to the demands of the labour market. The degree course is taught in English at the       
University of Camerino.

tissue models, for pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and biomedical research.We provide custom research
services, preclinical testing solutions, and contract research (CRO) services to support drug
discovery, toxicity testing, and offer reliable alternatives to animal testing.**

### **For a better human world**

## About us

CTIBIOTECH™, leveraging **NAM (Novel Alternative Models)**, specializes in the development of
advanced 2D and 3D human tissue models, including tumor models and organoids, for pharmaceutical and
cosmetic applications. **NAM’s** approach enhances our **in vitro** and **ex vivo** platforms,
designed for drug screening, toxicity testing, and oncology research, supporting preclinical
development with predictive and human-relevant data. We also provide custom model development and
contract research services (CRO) tailored to the needs of biotech and pharmaceutical companies.

At CTIBIOTECH™, we believe in innovation for a healthier future. Our goal is to create accurate and
reliable human tissues that enable researchers and companies to better understand diseases, test
drugs, and develop new treatments. We use cutting-edge technologies, such as stem cells and 3D
printing, to create 3D tissue and cell models that realistically simulate the structure and function
of human tissues.

###### **Buy cells and tissues**

Our biobank-derived human cells and tissues, including skin, hair, blood, and stem cells, support in
vitro and ex vivo drug testing, cosmetic and pharmaceutical product development, efficacy

custom biosourcing services to help biotech and pharmaceutical companies accelerate innovation.

# Services

#### ESG DATA MANAGEMENT AS A SERVICE
* #### Design & Strategy
  
  Get tailored project management support for initiatives, including - developing an ESG data
  governance and pipeline strategy, designing a cost effective IT architecture for ESG data
  management, implementing custom solutions to manage your ESG data.
* #### Data Collection
  
  Project management support for initiatives including - aggregating ESG data sources, stakeholder
  engagement and coordination, automating primary data collection, implementing continuous data
  collection processes, and integrating ESG data into standard business processes and workflows.
* #### Data Processing
  
  Project support for buidling ESG data models and pipelines, Data definition manuals, ESG data
  transformation (ETL),
* #### Data Represenation
  
  Reporting and disclosure, Impact dashboards,

#### MATERIALITY ANALYSIS AS A SERVICE
* #### Value Chain & Stakeholder Analysis
  
  Map value chain, identify stakeholders, generate material topics
* #### IRO Identification & Analysis
  
  Identify, categorize and analyse impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs) quantify financial
  materiality of risks, assess materiality based on stakeholder feedback.
* #### Materiality Matrix Development
  
  Identify materiality thresholds, create materiality matrix, map data points to business strategy,
  plan communication with stakeholders.

#### SUSTAINABILITY IMPLEMENTATION AS A SERVICE
* #### Frameworks & Standards
  
  Comprehensive project support for target-setting initiatives like SBTi and CDP, reporting and
  disclosure initiatives like CSRD, GRI and sector-specific frameworks.
* #### Carbon Accounting
  
  Organisational and product carbon accounting initiatives, including scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG
  inventory, product carbon footprinting, product lifecycle analysis (LCA) etc.
* #### Climate Mitigation & Adaptation
  
  Design, planning and implementation of climate mitigation and adaptation projects including,
  energy efficiency, decarbonization, circular economy, carbon abatement and climate investments.

# Color Meanings – Discover the Power and Symbolism Behind Every Hue

[Color Meanings]

Colors play an exceptionally prominent role in our lives. They influence our thinking, inspire our
decision-making, and impact our moods. From causing changes to changing reactions, colors are more
powerful than we think. Depending on our interpretations, they can be used for both good and evil.
Fortunately, we have the power to welcome some colors and shun others. This guide will take you on a
journey through the exciting universe of color meanings.

It’s important to note that not all colors were created equal. Though some shades are similar, that
doesn’t mean they’ll awaken the same emotions. To truly grasp the meaning of color, we must learn to
accept this. It’s also imperative to relinquish some control. Try as we might, we won’t always have
a handle on our emotions. Colors have such a substantial effect on the mind and body, and until we
make our peace with this reality, we’ll remain forever perplexed by inexplicable and random
reactions.

## Recognizing Your Responses

Have you ever noticed a shift in your attitude while surrounded by a particular color? Perhaps
you’ve been overwhelmed with nostalgia while staring at a specific shade. You’ve likely written
these occurrences off as a common human response, but the cause is far more complex than that. Color
psychology teaches us that much of human behavior is dictated by color. When we open our minds to
this possibility, we begin to understand the scope of our perceptions.

Once we acknowledge that colors influence doings, it makes way for personal interpretations. In
other words, we level the playing field by regaining some control of how we react to colors. You may
realize that the color red triggers anger. To avoid unnecessary bouts of rage, limit your encounters
with this hue. On the other hand, yellow might make you feel cheery and upbeat. If so, introduce
more of this color into your life. With a healthy dose of awareness, you can somewhat manage the
moods and emotions that colors produce.

The psychology behind color is fascinating and ever-expanding. With that said, new meanings are
always coming to light. The more knowledge we acquire, the more informed we become. This prospect

fixed explanations, these findings can always shift. This fact is both unsettling and reassuring. As
researchers continue to delve into the many facets of the color wheel, new information is
continually revealing itself.

## What is a HTML color code?

A HTML color code is an identifier used to represent a color on the web and within other digital
assets. Common color codes are in the forms of: a keyword name, a hexadecimal value, a RGB (red,
green, blue) triplet, or a HSL (hue, saturation, lightness) triplet. Different values allow for
16,777,216 potential colors to be chosen.

For example, the color red can be identifier using the following formats:
* red (keyword name)
* #ff0000 (hex)
* (255,0,0) (RGB)
* (0, 100%, 50%) (HSL)

Because there are so many colors to choose from, tools have been created to make the task of
selection much simpler. A color picker allows a user to select a color by clicking on visual range
of color to pin-point an exact code. A color chart provides a listing of common colors for quick
selection.

To use a selected color code within your web page, you could place the following attribute within a
given element to change its background color to red: `style="background-color: #ff0000;"`

## What are HTML color codes used for?

HTML color codes are used within HTML and CSS to create web design color schemes. They are primarily
used by web designers, graphic designers, computer programmers, and digital illustrators. Choosing
the correct web colors can be exhausting, but it is a great skill to have, especially for marketing
purposes.

To read more about html colors, Wikipedia has a good resource on web colors:
[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_colors][27].

## Overview of tools

[Technology Centre Mapping]

# [Technology Centre Mapping][54]

Technology Centres help SMEs cross the 'Valley of Death' and go from lab to market to develop and
produce new technology-based products. They help companies reduce the time-to-market for new
innovation ideas. The EMI technology centre mapping helps businesses locate technology centres
across the EU that can address their needs.

[EU Reports]

# [EU Reports][55]

The goal of the EMI EU report is to provide an overview about the green and digital transition of
industrial ecosystems and progress made over time. The report draws conclusions regarding the EU's
competitive standing in advanced-technology-driven ecosystems when compared to its primary global
rivals. The first EU report will be launched soon.

[International Reports]

# [International Reports][56]

International reports explore the positioning of third countries regarding the development and
implementation of advanced technologies across industrial ecosystems. The EMI international reports
are currently in development and will be published on this page when they are finalised.

[EU Member State Factsheets]

# [EU Member State Factsheets][57]

The EU Member State factsheets present key findings about the state-of-play of the green and digital
transition in each of the EU’s 27 Member States, based on patent, production, investment, and trade
data collected within the framework of the EMI project. The 27 EU Member State factsheets are now
available.

[Technology Centre Reports]

# [Technology Centre Reports][58]

Technology Centres, and the technology infrastructures they host, offer a wide range of services
such as access to technology expertise and facilities, demonstration, prototype development and
testing, among others, which make them vital actors to realise industrial policy objectives.
However, this contribution is not always visible. The EMI project has therefore produced two reports
which describe the role of Technology Centres in the development of innovation ecosystems and their
added value in addressing the needs of industry. These reports will be made available soon.

[Other Reports]

# Our certifications

OEKO-TEX® standards enable everyone to make responsible decisions and protect natural resources.
Driven by sustainability and a dedication to transparency, our work is grounded in proven science.
Explore our portfolio [here][69] or apply for your chosen certification or service. 

[
[OEKO-TEX® MADE IN GREEN certification]

The MADE IN GREEN label identifies textiles and leather goods tested for harmful substances and
which have been manufactured under sustainable and socially responsible conditions.

][70]
[
[OEKO-TEX® STANDARD 100 certification]

All types of textiles that have been tested for harmful substances, from yarns to the finished
product, may bear the STANDARD 100 product label.

][71]
[
[OEKO-TEX® ORGANIC COTTON certification]

The ORGANIC COTTON certification offers verification from farm to product. Products bearing this
label have been tested for the use of genetically modified organisms (GMOs) and harmful substances.
 

][72]
[
[OEKO-TEX® LEATHER STANDARD certification]

The LEATHER STANDARD label is tailored to leather articles which have been tested for harmful
substances. Certification can be awarded for leather semi-finished products, finished leather,
leather fibre materials up to finished articles and accessories.

][73]
[
[OEKO-TEX® STeP certification]

STeP certifies production facilities which manufacture textile and leather articles under
sustainable production conditions.

][74]
[
[OEKO-TEX® ECO PASSPORT certification]

The ECO PASSPORT identifies chemicals, colourants and auxiliaries used in the textile and leather
industry which are not harmful to health and which are environmentally friendly.

RESPONSIBLE BUSINESS supports you on preventing or mitigating existing and potential negative
impacts of business operations within your own activities, your supply chains and your wider
business relationships.

substances. Certification can be awarded for leather semi-finished products, finished leather,
leather fibre materials up to finished articles and accessories.

industry which are not harmful to health and which are environmentally friendly.

Science, Technology and Innovation
Science, technology and innovation (STI) are essential for advancing the SDGs, enabling
evidence-based decision-making, accelerating implementation, and scaling solutions to complex global
challenges. On 6-7 May 2026, the eleventh annual Multi-Stakeholder Forum on Science, Technology and

Global Sustainable Development Report
The Global Sustainable Development Report (GSDR) is a United Nations publication aiming to
strengthen the science-policy interface, produced once every four years to inform the quadrennial
SDG review deliberations. The next report is scheduled for release in September 2027 ahead of the
High-level Political Forum on sustainable development to be held under the auspices of the General
Assembly (SDG Summit). [Global Sustainable Development Report][77] [GSDR in 2027][78] [GSDR in
2023][79]
Energy
Achieving SDG7 will open a new world of opportunities for millions of people through new economic
opportunities and jobs, empowered women, children and youth, better education and health, more
sustainable, equitable and inclusive communities, and greater protections from, and resilience to,
climate change. [Energy Compacts][80] [More on Energy][81]
Sustainable Transport
While there is no single dedicated Sustainable Development Goal for transport, it is reflected in
several SDG targets and recognized as an enabler for achieving many of the goals. The United Nations
Decade of Sustainable Transport will be an opportunity to further raise awareness of transport’s
crucial role in advancing the Sustainable Development Goals and to gather and rally new solutions,
resources and partnerships to advance sustainable transport globally. [UN Decade of Sustainable
Transport 2026 – 2035][82] [More on Sustainable Transport][83]
Water
Water is fundamental to sustainable development, underpinning health, food security, energy,
ecosystems, and economic growth. Ensuring universal access to safe drinking water and sanitation,
improving water quality, strengthening water management, and enhancing resilience to water-related
risks are essential for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and addressing climate change
impacts. The 2026 UN Water Conference will take place from 2–4 December 2026 in the United Arab
Emirates. Co-hosted by Senegal and the United Arab Emirates, the Conference aims to accelerate the
implementation of SDG 6 on clean water and sanitation, strengthen global water governance, and
further elevate water-related issues on the international agenda through concrete action and
partnerships. [2026 UN Water Conference][84] [More on Water and Sanitation][85]

# Quebec, Your Destination of Choice for Accelerating Your Clinical Research Projects

### Quebec is proposing a fast, reliable and stable clinical research environment that is aligned
### with rigorous pharmaceutical industry standards in order to support the success of your projects
### and help realize your ambitions.

A [G7 leader][33] in clinical research, Canada has the greatest number of clinical trials
proportionately to its population. Quebec plays a key role as participant in [more than 40%][34] of
all clinical research projects carried out across Canada. Through the expertise of its teams and the
excellence of its health care system, Quebec stands out in all treatment fields and for all
indications.

## Learn About What Makes up Quebec’s Strength in Clinical Research

A highly efficient environment for faster clinical trial start-up Quebec offers an efficient
pan-Canadian regulatory framework, allowing Health Canada to approve a clinical trial application
within 30 days, and a [FAST TRACK Evaluation Service][38] aimed at approving clinical research
trials in 8 weeks in public institutions, which is about 75 % faster than the usual standard
timeframes found worldwide.

[World-class sites and investigators][39], [specialized contractual organizations][40], as well as [
patient organizations][41] driving the performance and quality of your projects.

Through its considerable ethnic diversity and some specific genetic characteristics inherited from a
small number of original inhabitants (called the “founder effect”), Quebec provides a unique context
for advancing research, particularly on rare diseases, orphan diseases and precision medicine. This
strength is maintained by a network of centres of excellence in rare diseases.

[
[icon-14182]

International recognition of clinical data in Quebec

][42]
[
[icon-14184]

][43]
[
[icon-14186]

Attractive tax incentives and credits

][44]

The trials conducted in Quebec observe Good Clinical Practices (GCP) and international standards,
ensuring that data generated are acceptable to agencies such as the FDA (USA) and EMA (Europe),
which facilitates access to world markets.

In the heart of one of the largest integrated health systems in North America, Quebec provides
[strategic access to anonymized health data for public and private research][45]. This access
enables faster and more precise clinical research that is rooted in real-world conditions, stepping
up the development and assessment of cutting-edge innovations.

Companies benefit from a provincial tax credit of up to 64 % of eligible salaries and 33 % of
subcontracting costs associated with scientific research and experimental development, in addition
to the federal tax credit. This tax support considerably reduces the total cost of pharmaceutical
development and medical technology projects.

development and medical technology projects.

within 30 days, and a [FAST TRACK Evaluation Service][47] aimed at approving clinical research
trials in 8 weeks in public institutions, which is about 75 % faster than the usual standard
timeframes found worldwide.

[icon-14180]

A unique demographic and genetic profile

][52]

Through its considerable ethnic diversity and some specific genetic characteristics inherited from a
small number of original inhabitants (called the “founder effect”), Quebec provides a unique context
for advancing research, particularly on rare diseases, orphan diseases and precision medicine. This
strength is maintained by a network of centres of excellence in rare diseases.

[
[icon-14182]

International recognition of clinical data in Quebec

][53]

ensuring that data generated are acceptable to agencies such as the FDA (USA) and EMA (Europe),
which facilitates access to world markets.

Access to health data from a major integrated public network

[strategic access to anonymized health data for public and private research][55]. This access
enables faster and more precise clinical research that is rooted in real-world conditions, stepping
up the development and assessment of cutting-edge innovations.

Attractive tax incentives and credits

to the federal tax credit. This tax support considerably reduces the total cost of pharmaceutical

Don't want to be distrupted? Want to take a brake? Use a white screen to blank your screen.

To get a source of light and be able to read books when it’s dark in the room and the light switch
is too far away.

As a bright light source for doing makeup or taking pictures

## white screen to clean monitor

Silly, but I use it for monitor cleaning. It makes things on the screen obvious. :) I also use it to
validate plain colour reproduction for different monitors, but that only comes up rarely and I'm not
looking for professional colour grading.

Consistent backdrop to clean my monitor on, and also to check for dead/stuck pixels. Also sometimes
for lighting my face when I'm using a webcam.

I was catching little flies as they were attracted to white screen on my display

I'm working on a animated sequence, and i'm doing it the traditional way (by hand), so i need a
white surface with light that allows me to put one piece of paper over another and be able to see
both, so since i don't have a professional screen for this, i'm using my computer and putting the
white screen on it so i don't touch anything by mistake

When I am not searching, I put the white screen so I don't get distracted with anything on the
computer

Useful when adjusting settings in my secondary monitor (since it's quite old it doesn't just set
stuff how it should be by default). Settings like vertical/horizontal position and
vertical/horizontal scale. Also useful when searching for dead pixels.

## white screen to draw at night

If I'm drawing on paper, I can put paper on top of my display drawing tablet and see what I'm
drawing at night
